jobs.occupation: Experienced Waiters – Ristorante Porto Sociale
jobs.description:
Waiters Wanted – Join the New Porto Sociale in Oslo!
Be part of an exciting new chapter in Italian hospitality! Porto Sociale, an Italian restaurant in the heart of Oslo, is preparing for an exciting relaunch. With a major renovation, a refreshed concept, and ambitious plans for the future, we aim to create one of Oslo's most exciting Italian dining destinations. Our vision is to combine authentic Italian cuisine, exceptional wines, and warm, personal service in an elegant yet welcoming atmosphere.

 

We are now looking for passionate and service-minded waiters who want to help us create memorable dining experiences and become part of our new team.
Your responsibilities
• Provide professional, attentive, and personalized service to our guests.
• Welcome guests, present menus, and take food and beverage orders.
• Recommend dishes, wines, and other beverages based on guests' preferences.
• Ensure smooth and efficient service throughout the dining experience.
• Work closely with the kitchen, bar, and management team.
• Maintain high standards of presentation, cleanliness, and organization.
• Contribute to a positive working environment and an exceptional guest experience.Who are we looking for?
• Previous experience as a waiter, preferably from quality restaurants, fine dining, or premium hospitality.
• A genuine passion for hospitality and creating memorable guest experiences.
• Good knowledge of food and beverages, particularly wine.
• An interest in Italian cuisine, wines, and culture.
• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
• A professional, positive, and outgoing personality.
• Ability to remain organized and deliver excellent service during busy periods.
• Strong teamwork skills and a willingness to learn.
• Good English communication skills. Norwegian or Italian is an advantage.
• Flexibility to work evenings and weekends.
We value personality, attitude, and genuine enthusiasm for hospitality just as much as experience.
What we offer
• The opportunity to be part of an exciting restaurant relaunch in central Oslo.
• A newly renovated restaurant with ambitious plans for the future.
• A professional and welcoming working environment.
• The chance to work with authentic Italian cuisine and quality wines.
• Training and opportunities to develop your knowledge of Italian food, wine, and hospitality.
• Opportunities for professional growth and increased responsibility.
• Competitive salary based on experience and qualifications.
• The chance to help shape the service culture of the new Porto Sociale.Interested?
Are you passionate about hospitality, enjoy working with people, and want to be part of something exciting?

We would love to hear from you!

 

Send us your CV and a short introduction about yourself, your experience, and why you would like to join Porto Sociale.

 

Join us and help create an Italian dining experience that guests will remember!

Om arbeidsgiveren:

Located in Aker Brygge, Oslo, Porto Sociale is an Italian restaurant preparing for an exciting new chapter. With a major renovation, a refreshed concept, and ambitious plans for the future, we aim to create one of Oslo’s most exciting Italian dining destinations. Our vision is to combine authentic Italian traditions with high-quality ingredients, exceptional food, and warm, personal service. From outstanding pizza and handmade pasta to carefully prepared seafood, meat, and regional Italian specialties, we want to showcase the very best of Italian cuisine.

jobs.occupation: Are you our new Mechanical Designer?
jobs.description:
Join us in shaping the next generation of maritime technology. We are looking for a Mechanical Designer to strengthen our hardware organization and develop robust, functional and manufacturable solutions for maritime applications. In this role, you will turn requirements and ideas into mechanical designs, contributing from early concepts through detailed design, prototyping and production follow-up.

We are looking for someone who combines practical mechanical understanding with an interest in product development. If you enjoy 3D modelling, solving design challenges and working with materials and manufacturing processes—and preferably have an interest in maritime applications—we would love to hear from you.

As a Mechanical Designer, you will develop mechanical parts, assemblies, enclosures and mounting solutions as part of a multidisciplinary team. You will collaborate with hardware engineers, product management, suppliers and production to ensure that design meets requirements for functionality, quality, assembly and serviceability throughout the product lifecycle.

If you enjoy combining creative design with structured engineering and hands-on problem-solving, this role could be a great fit for you.

 

Key accountabilities

• Develop concepts, 3D CAD models and detailed mechanical designs for parts and assemblies.
• Prepare and maintain production drawings, bills of materials and technical documentation, including tolerances and material specifications.
• Select materials, surface treatments and manufacturing methods, considering corrosion resistance, cost, quality and environmental requirements.
• Collaborate with suppliers and production to optimise designs for manufacturing, assembly and serviceability.
• Participate in design reviews, prototype builds and verification testing, following up findings and design improvements.
• Support existing products through mechanical design updates, engineering changes and resolution of production and field issues.
 

This employment may require a pre-employment check procedure in accordance with company security standards, role or site requirements. Please note that this might affect the offer process or employment.

This employment requires security clearance by the Norwegian National Security Authority. The successful candidate may start work with limited accesses whilst the clearance is being processed. Please note that this might affect the offer process or employment.

Qualifications and experience

• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree, or technical college qualification, in Mechanical Engineering, Mechanical Design, Product Development or a related field. We encourage 2026 graduates to apply.
• Proficiency in 3D CAD modelling and preparation of technical drawings, gained through studies, projects or professional experience.
• Knowledge of dimensioning, geometrical tolerancing (GD&T), tolerance analysis and design for manufacturing and assembly.
• Good English communication, written and verbal.
• Understanding materials, surface treatments and manufacturing processes such as sheet metal fabrication and machining.
• Familiarity with product data or lifecycle management systems (PLM), bills of materials and revision control is an advantage.
• Experience with maritime or industrial equipment, prototyping, mechanical testing or structural analysis is an advantage.
At Kongsberg Maritime, we believe that diversity fuels innovation. We encourage you to apply, even if you do not meet every requirement. Your unique perspective is valuable to us. Your skills, attitude and perspective could be exactly what we are looking for!

 

You are able to

• act on own initiative, make things happen and accept responsibility for the results.
• demonstrate specialist knowledge and expertise in own area.
• communicate in a clear, precise, and structured way.
• co-operate well with others, share knowledge, experience, information, and support others in the pursuit of team goals.
 

What we can offer you

• An exciting and important position working for the world-leading supplier of maritime solutions.
• Professional development and career opportunities.
• Competitive terms including attractive insurance policies and pension schemes.
• We offer flexible working hours and the option to work remote or from home office.
• Social welfare club with social and recreational activities.
 

Work location Ålesund, Kongsberg or Horten.

Point of contact Terje Lehn Karlsen, +47 958 85 060

Kongsberg Maritime is a global leader in maritime technology. We deliver advanced solutions to the merchant fleet, offshore, fishing, and naval vessels, setting new standards for safe, efficient, and sustainable operations - both for new builds and existing fleets. In close collaboration with customers and research environments, we develop technology that solves real challenges at sea. Today, more than 30,000 vessels operate with our systems on board. Kongsberg Maritime has more than 8,300 employees in 35 countries.

jobs.occupation: Talent Acquisition Partner (Maternity Cover)
jobs.description:
Working at Mercell 
At Mercell, we're on a mission to revolutionize public procurement, making it accessible and effortless for everyone involved. Imagine a world where public buyers and visionary suppliers come together seamlessly to make a great deal easier and shape the future. That's what we're all about.

With a dynamic culture built on continuous growth, trust, and collaboration, Mercell offers an environment where your talents can thrive. You will be part of an international environment with ambitious and dedicated colleagues who are passionate about what they do and supported to be themselves.

Together, let's shape the future and create real value for society, one innovative solution at a time.

Your Mission 
As the Talent Acquisition Partner, you'll be the driving force behind attracting, assessing and nurturing top talent that fuels Mercell's success. Your mission is to leverage our recruitment strategy, ensuring that we continue building diverse, skilled, and dynamic teams across Mercell in all different functions and locations. This is an opportunity to make a lasting impact on Mercell's growth story and contribute to shaping the future of our organisation with your passion for talent.

We see the following qualities as important to thrive in this role:

• 
Proactive and agile with a creative mindset

• 
Strong in stakeholder management including collaboration with senior leadership

• 
Able to take ownership and multitask effectively

• 
Self driven and structured

Core Responsibilities  
• 
Full lifecycle recruitment: Lead end-to-end recruitment processes, from identifying talent needs to sourcing, interviewing, and onboarding exceptional individuals.

• 
Review resumes and credentials for appropriateness of skills, experience, and knowledge in relation to position requirements.

• 
Source candidates by utilizing cutting-edge technology, social media and targeted networking.

• 
Develop, regularly update and maintain the recruitment database.

• 
Stakeholder collaboration: Work closely with hiring managers and leadership to understand business needs, ensuring a strategic and collaborative approach to talent acquisition.

• 
Innovative recruitment techniques: Implement creative and effective recruitment methods, staying ahead of industry trends to attract top-tier talent.

Required Qualifications  
• 
Proven experience (ideally 3-5 years) in Talent Acquisition or in a similar recruitment role.

• 
Demonstrated success in managing effectively multiple recruitment processes while ensuring the best candidate and hiring manager experience.

• 
Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills.

• 
In-depth knowledge of interviewing, recruitment best practices and industry trends in multiple sectors such as tech, finance, commercial, product.

• 
Strong experience with LinkedIN as hiring tool.

• 
Experience in sourcing various profiles.

• 
Fluent in written and spoken English.

Preferred Qualifications  

• 
Experience in competency based interviewing (CBI).

• 
Previous experience in tech or SaaS recruitment is a plus.

• 
Familiarity with HR best practices, technologies and tools as well as AI tools such as Claude.

• 
Employer branding experience.

 

Start date: Approximately by January/February 2027 

Duration: Full time (minimum 80%) - Temporary Maternity Cover (around 1 year) 

Workplace type: Hybrid - working onsite at the office min. 3 days and from home, balancing flexibility with collaboration 

Location: Oslo, Norway 

Application Deadline: 06 December 2026. However, do not wait to submit your application - we will read applications and talk to potential candidates as we receive them 

 
What we offer 
As a fast growing technology company, we are committed to taking care of our employees through initiatives such as hybrid work to support work-life balance, health and insurance plans (may differ per country/office), pension plans, paid parental leave, social happenings and competitive salary packages. Please see https://career.mercell.com/pages/perks-benefits to get more insights on what to expect of perks, benefits and culture when joining Mercell.

Has this sparked your interest?
Then we can't wait to have you join our mission and looking forward to receiving your application!

-Mercell is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds and experiences.

-Mercell handles all personal data in line with GDPR and our Privacy Policy.

-Mercell does not provide relocation support. We are seeking candidates who are already based in, or have existing work authorization for, the country where the role is located.

-Mercell may carry out background checks on applicants to verify information that appears on CVs and other documentation. This background check is carried out by an external party and is not carried out without the consent of the applicant. Current applicants will receive further information about this.

Om arbeidsgiveren:
At Mercell, we’re transforming how businesses manage procurement and public tendering processes. As a leading provider of digital solutions for procurement, we help organizations across Europe streamline, automate, and optimize their sourcing operations. Our cloud-based platform connects buyers and suppliers, driving transparency, efficiency, and compliance in public and private sector procurement.

The Problem We Solve:
Procurement is often plagued by inefficiencies, manual workflows, and a lack of transparency, making it time-consuming and prone to errors. This not only impacts operational performance but can also prevent businesses from making strategic, cost-effective decisions. At Mercell, we are solving these challenges by providing an integrated solution that simplifies the tendering process, ensures compliance with regulatory standards, and empowers businesses with data-driven insights.

Why We Do It: 
We believe that efficient procurement is at the heart of sustainable business growth. By digitizing and optimizing the procurement process, we help organizations save time, reduce costs, and make smarter decisions, all while fostering a more competitive and transparent marketplace. Our goal is to empower organizations to focus on their core business, leaving procurement complexity to us.

At Mercell, we’re driven by innovation and a passion to continuously improve the procurement landscape.

jobs.occupation: PhD Research Scholar positions - Department of Finance
jobs.description:
The PhD specialisation
NHH is pleased to announce openings in the PhD specialisation in Finance. Candidates admitted to the PhD programme will receive the title of PhD Research Scholar.

The Department of Finance has 23 faculty members, two-thirds of whom are international. Research at the department spans all major fields of finance, including corporate finance, asset pricing, and financial intermediation. Faculty regularly publish in the top academic journals and are one of the leading finance groups in Europe. The department has an active research seminar series featuring invited top scholars and an internal brown bag seminar series.

The PhD specialisation in Finance gives PhD research scholars the theoretical knowledge and methodological skills necessary to become successful researchers. It combines a one-year intensive course portfolio with ample time to do research and write a dissertation. PhD research scholars work closely with their thesis advisors and receive feedback by presenting their research in internal seminars. The department offers a stimulating research environment and encourages PhD research scholars to participate in its many research activities. We have a strong record of placing graduates in international academic institutions. Research and conference travels are strongly encouraged and funding for these purposes is usually available. The Department of Finance is well connected internationally and is a member of the Nordic Finance Network. Many of our PhD research scholars spend a semester or a year abroad visiting another university. The PhD specialisation in Finance, which has a total of 10 to 12 PhD research scholars, is an important integrated part of the department’s research environment. 

See the department’s website here: Department of Finance | NHH

Start date: August 2027
The PhD programme
The PhD programme at NHH is a four-year fully-funded programme, which combines an intensive course component and research, preparing the school’s graduates for scholarly positions at reputable research institutions and positions in knowledge-intensive organisations both within and outside academia. Former PhD graduates have been hired by renowned institutions such as Harvard University, The University of Sydney’s Business School, University of Amsterdam, University of St. Gallen, Tilburg University, Stockholm School of Economics, Copenhagen Business School, Hanken School of Economics, Norwegian universities and business schools, as well as by government, banking, finance and consulting industries.

The PhD research scholars will be included in a highly stimulating and rewarding research environment, working closely with faculty members and fellow PhD research scholars. PhD research scholars participate actively in faculty and research seminars, as well as in workshops. As part of the position, the PhD research scholars allocate 25% of their time to career promoting work such as teaching assistance. They also receive pedagogical training. The place of work is at NHH in Bergen, where the PhD research scholars will have their own office space at their department.

The PhD programme gives preference to applicants who address research questions that align with the department’s research interests and the available resources for supervision. As the school aspires gender balance and diversity, female applicants will be given preference if applicants are otherwise equally qualified.
NHH offers
• annual salary of NOK 600 000 (equivalent to approximately EUR 55 946 or USD 61 457) pr. August 2027. For particularly well-qualified applicants, a higher salary may be considered. Thereafter annual adjustment of minimum 3%. The salary ensures a fair standard of living in Norway and is subject to Norwegian taxes and benefits, including public health care benefits and pension savings
• career guidance and an individual career development plan
• opportunity to take basic Norwegian language courses
• research funds for travels and funding for conference participation and research stays abroad to build a wider network and strengthen the research of the PhD research scholar
Bergen provides a vibrant cultural scene with easy access to mountains, fjords and a wide range of outdoor activities. The city offers a family-friendly environment and was ranked the best city in Europe for quality of life in Oxford Economics’ 2026 Global Cities Index. Most public services, like healthcare and schools are free in Norway. To explore Norway and the city of Bergen, go to visitnorway.com.
Eligibility requirements
Applicants must meet the eligibility requirements for the PhD programme. Applicants must normally have completed a five-year Master of Science (MSc) degree in Economics and Business Administration or a comparable degree. The average grade must normally correspond to a minimum of B (4.0) in the Norwegian grade system. 

The Department of Finance requires you to demonstrate both an adequate level of academic skills and an adequate level of English language proficiency (unless you are exempt). We accept the following tests:

• GMAT or GRE tests to measure your academic skills
• TOEFL, IELTS or PTE Academic to measure your English language proficiency
When applying, you are required to upload a copy of your unofficial test scores in Jobbnorge before the deadline. If you are shortlisted, NHH will ask you to give us access to your official test scores without delay.

Exemptions:

• You are waived from the GMAT or GRE tests if you hold a qualifying master’s degree from a Nordic institution.
• You are waived from TOEFL, IELTS or PTE Academic tests if you are a native English speaker, if you have a qualifying master’s degree from a Nordic institution or if you have a qualifying master’s degree where the language of tuition was English.
For more detailed information about the tests and their minimum scores, please visit our webpage: Admission to the PhD programme| NHH. If you have questions, you may contact phd@nhh.no.
Application requirements
You are required to upload the following documents with your application in Jobbnorge:

• Certificate of your master’s degree or equivalent, including transcripts of records. You need to have completed your master’s degree prior to the starting date for the position. If you have not completed your degree when applying for the position, please attach a transcript of records of the courses and grades that you have completed so far.
• Certificate of your bachelor’s degree or equivalent, including transcripts of records.
• Other relevant certificates or transcripts (e.g. courses completed at the PhD level).
• If the issuing authority of grades and degrees does not use the ECTS grading scale, include an official description of the grading scale used.
• Statement of purpose describing your motivation for applying for this position (250-300 words).
• A research proposal (2000-4000 words). The research proposal should describe the aims, research questions, and motivation of the proposed research. Please note that your research proposal is tentative and often needs adjustments after your acceptance into the programme. 
• Curriculum vitae.
• A list of all publications and/or other documented research activities.   
Please upload the documents in separate files, not combined in one single file.

Letters of recommendation and contact details of references:

Letters of recommendation and/or contact details of references may strengthen your application, but they are not mandatory. If you choose to include letters of recommendations, the references should send their letter of recommendation in PDF format to hr-phd@nhh.no by latest 15 January 2027. Contact details of references may be included in Jobbnorge when you apply. 
General information
For more information on the PhD programme and the submission procedure, please consult the NHH PhD website. Incomplete applications will not be considered.

Please note that applicants for the PhD research scholar position do not need to apply separately for admission to the PhD programme.

NHH emphasises diversity and encourages qualified candidates to apply for the position regardless of gender, age, disability and cultural background.

In accordance with §25 (2) of the Freedom of Information Act, information about applicants may be made public even if they have requested not to have their names entered on the list of applicants. Applicants will be notified if their request is not granted.
 
As part of the recruitment process, a background check may be conducted with the candidates' consent.

For questions and inquiries about the NHH PhD programme, please contact phd@nhh.no.

Applications must be submitted through the Jobbnorge online portal. To open the application, please click ‘Apply for this job’. For the English version, go to the menu at the top right side.

Application deadline: 15 January 2027

jobs.occupation: PhD Research Scholar positions - Department of Economics
jobs.description:
The PhD specialisation
NHH is pleased to announce vacancies in the PhD specialisation in Economics. Candidates admitted to the PhD programme will receive the title of PhD Research Scholar. 

We are looking for candidates in all fields of economics. Women are particularly encouraged to apply. 

The Department of Economics is looking for highly motivated and talented individuals. The PhD specialisation in Economics aims to give graduates rigorous training in conducting high-quality scientific research in economics, making use of state-of-the-art empirical and theoretical techniques. The PhD programme prepares PhD research scholars for the international academic job market, for positions at national and international policy institutions, central banks, research organisations, and industry. 

The Department of Economics offers an international and research-active environment with 45 faculty members and 30 PhD research scholars in various fields. The Department encourages interaction between PhD research scholars and faculty through social gatherings, seminars, and workshops in which PhD research scholars are fully involved. 

In addition to the training described above, PhD research scholars are integrated into the Department’s international research network and are provided with personal computers, printing facilities, extensive library resources, and a wide range of software.

jobs.description:
The PhD specialisation
NHH is pleased to announce vacancies in the Department of Strategy and Management. Candidates admitted to the PhD program will receive the title of PhD Research Scholar. The department welcomes applications specialising in several fields of research such as strategy, innovation, management, organizational behaviour, and marketing. The research areas described below represent research opportunities emphasised by the Department, but applications within other relevant research areas are also welcome.

Start date: August 2027Digital Innovation for sustainable GrowthDigital Innovation for sustainable Growth (DIG) is a research center at the Department of Strategy and Management, focusing on sustainable growth and transformation enabled by digital technologies. As a PhD Research Scholar, you will join an ambitious research community with access to leading organizations, national register data, and advanced AI infrastructure. We invite applications on the following major grand challenges: AI for Business and the Silver Economy. AI is reshaping organizations, strategies, and workforce skills, while demographic aging creates both challenges and opportunities for business innovation and sustainable growth. These shifts call for new insights into strategy, competition, and organizational adaptation.

The center’s research focuses primarily on five key areas:

• Business intelligence
• Consumer Psychology and Technology Adoption
• Creating and capturing sustainable value
• Governance Leadership and Change
• Future of Work
Applications within all these areas are welcome. E-mail: bram.timmermans@nhh.no or lasse.lien@nhh.no

Global Strategy / International Business – with a focus on digital transformation and geopoliticsGlobal Strategy investigates how the global context shapes firms’ strategies and strategic management. Recent geopolitical events, rising populism that weakens global institutions, and the urgency of grand social and environmental challenges are redrawing that context and creating rich research opportunities. In parallel, advances in digital technologies - including AI and Industry 4.0 - challenge core assumptions in International Business, reshaping where firms expand, how they organize cross-border activities, and how they compete. We welcome proposals that explore these themes and their intersections using primarily quantitative methods. We are explicitly open to candidates from adjacent disciplines - such as political science, international relations, or information systems - who seek to integrate their perspectives to advance Global Strategy and International Business research.E-mail: bjorn.schmeisser@nhh.no

Productive Alone but Wiser Together? AI and Collective Knowledge Building in OrganizationsMeeting, learning from, and sharing with colleagues is central to how organizations build collective knowledge. As employees increasingly turn to AI and large language models as sparring partners, these interactions may be quietly displaced. Organizations want to encourage AI use for productivity and efficiency, yet they also need to preserve the organic social interactions through which collective knowledge is built. Early evidence highlights this tension: AI assistance can raise individual performance while narrowing the knowledge groups draw on, and contributions to public knowledge-sharing communities have fallen since generative AI arrived. Far less is known about how this plays out inside organizations. The project will examine what organizations can do, and which work designs can help balance individual productivity with collective knowledge building in the age of AI. We especially welcome candidates interested in Information Systems, Systems Thinking or Organization Theory, and in qualitative research within organizations adopting AI.Email: vidya.oruganti@nhh.no

The Future of Human Resource Management (HRM)Rapid technological change is transforming how we work, organize, and lead. Remote and hybrid work, digital collaboration tools, and AI are creating new opportunities and challenges for organizations and employees. We invite PhD candidates to develop original research on these transformations in a Nordic context, where collaboration among employers, employees, and labor unions plays a central role. As a PhD Research Scholar, you will join an active research environment, work closely with experienced faculty, and contribute new knowledge about how technology is shaping HRM and the future of work.E-mail: karen.olsen@nhh.no

The Board of Directors (BoD) as Strategic Partner and Change AgentThe role of the Board of Directors has evolved from monitoring performance, controlling the financials and approving strategy to becoming increasingly involved in and responsible for the strategic direction of the firm, particularly as a partner to the top management team supporting strategic renewal and innovation in the established firm. Research questions of interest include: exploring the processes through which BoDs initiate and influence strategic change and renewal, the collaborative dynamics between BoDs and senior management, and internal board dynamics.E-mail: inger.stensaker@nhh.no

Teams and cooperationMuch of the value-creating work in organizations takes place in teams, from project and product teams to top management teams and corporate boards. We invite proposals that examine what makes teams work effectively, and how relationships, norms and patterns of interaction within teams form, develop and change over time. Possible areas include, but are not limited to:

• Team start-up and development: How do early interactions and launch processes shape later team dynamics and performance?
• Psychological safety: How does psychological safety emerge, vary and erode over time, and how does it relate to learning, error handling, voice and performance?
• Boards as teams: What characterizes boardroom dynamics? How do interpersonal processes in boards, such as trust, dissent, information sharing and the board–CEO relationship, affect board effectiveness and the quality of governance?
• Humans and AI in teams: What opportunities and challenges emerge when AI is integrated into teamwork? How does it change coordination, roles, trust and learning?
• Emotions in teams: What role do emotions and emotional dynamics play in team processes and performance?
We welcome a range of methodological approaches, including experiments, longitudinal field studies, qualitative research and multi-method designs. Applicants are encouraged to develop their own research questions within this broad area.E-mail: therese.egeland@nhh.no

Consumer trust in AI agentsArtificial intelligence is increasingly taking on roles traditionally performed by humans in marketing, including recommending products, generating advertising content, handling customer service interactions, and personalizing communications. As consumers encounter AI more frequently throughout the customer journey, researchers are seeking to understand how they perceive, evaluate, and respond to AI-based interactions. Key issues include consumer trust; perceived competence and warmth in AI systems; algorithm aversion versus algorithm appreciation; and the conditions under which consumers prefer AI agents over human employees. In this project, the main questions are: What factors facilitate trust in AI agents? Under what conditions do consumers prefer AI agents over human representatives for marketing-related tasks such as product recommendation, customer support, and service recovery?E-mail: magne.supphellen@nhh.no

Export brandingMany exporters in B2C and B2B markets use country-of-origin information in foreign-market communication. Previous research shows that such information can significantly affect brand evaluation and sales of export brands. Origin is often communicated as a simple extrinsic cue, for instance, through a made-in label. However, exporters can achieve greater leverage from origin by including favorable origin elements in export brand positioning. More research is needed on exporters' current practices and how they can leverage origin more effectively: To what extent do exporters include origin information in the brand positioning? When is this more and less effective? How is this practice different in B2B and B2C markets? What procedures do exporters use to integrate origin, and which normative, theory-based procedures can be developed?E-mail: magne.supphellen@nhh.no

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral position in Behavioral and Experimental Economics
jobs.description:
About the position
NHH in Bergen, Norway, invites applications for a postdoctoral position in behavioral and experimental economics at the Department of Economics, as part of the FAIR Markets research project funded by the European Research Council (Project 101267064). The duration of the position is three years.The postdoctoral position offers a unique opportunity to join an ambitious research environment in behavioral and experimental economics and to become an integral part of the FAIR – Centre for Experimental Research on Fairness, Inequality and Rationality and the Department of Economics (FAIR) at the Department of Economics.The successful candidate will join an ambitious new research agenda on the moral foundations of markets and work closely with Bertil Tungodden and other researchers at FAIR and The Choice Lab on projects combining experimental methods, large-scale surveys, and rich administrative data to study how people evaluate the fairness and legitimacy of market transactions. The position provides substantial scope for intellectual contribution and for developing independent research within the broader FAIR Markets agenda.
 
We are looking for a highly ambitious and collaborative researcher with a strong background in behavioral and experimental economics and a particular interest in questions related to fairness, markets, and public policy. The successful candidate should have excellent analytical and technical skills. The ideal candidate will combine methodological rigor with creativity and a strong motivation to contribute to high-quality research aimed at publication in leading international journals.The department seeks ambitious candidates early in their careers. Applicants should hold, or be close to completing, a PhD degree in a business-oriented field such as economics or a closely related field from a recognised business school or university.
NHH offers
• Competitive terms depending on the level of competence/length of service.
• An academically stimulating working environment.
• A favorable membership in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK) and good welfare benefits such as parental leave.
• Research funds for travel and conference participation, and a bonus system for publication in top international journals (up to NOK 200 000).
Note that public health care, public schooling for children, and most other public services are free in Norway. The city of Bergen has a mild, coastal climate and offers rich opportunities for culture and outdoor activities – as well as a family-friendly environment (explore visitnorway.com).
General information
The appointee must comply with the guidelines that apply to the position at any time.NHH emphasises diversity and encourages qualified candidates to apply for the position regardless of gender, age, disability and cultural background.In the assessment of applicants, international experience and qualifications will be emphasised. For the sake of gender balance at NHH, female applicants will be given preference in the event of equivalent qualifications among candidates.Applicants are requested to present a research statement with their application. The application should contain details of the applicant's scientific and pedagogical education and work experience. The application package, including a CV, certificates with grades, a maximum of 5 published or unpublished research papers, a complete list of published papers and papers in the pipeline, and any other relevant documentation, should be submitted through the Jobbnorge online portal. To open the application, please click 'Apply for this job'. For English version, go to the menu at the top right side.
 
Two or three reference letters (in PDF) must be submitted by the referees directly to NHH at hr-references@nhh.no, by latest 22 December 2026.

As part of the recruitment process, a background check may be conducted with the candidates' consent.

In accordance with §25 (2) of the Freedom of Information Act, information about applicants may be made public even if they have requested not to have their names entered on the list of applicants. Applicants will be notified if their request is not granted.

Enquiries about the position may be directed to:

• Professor Bertil Tungodden, by email: bertil.tungodden@nhh.no
• Administrative coordinator Mette Soltvedt, by email: mette.soltvedt@nhh.no
The deadline for applications is 22 December 2026. This date also applies to the submission of publications/written work.

jobs.occupation: Join NordicNeuroLab in developing electronics for the iMRI environment!
jobs.description:
NordicNeuroLab is expanding their work within interventional MRI (iMRI), and developing a communication system for these workflows.

 

As part of this initiative, we are building a dedicated engineering team, where we are looking for an experienced Hardware / Electronics Engineer to strengthen the iMRI team. In this role, you will take ownership of key technical challenges and help shape the solution, driving it from its current early stage towards a commercial product over the next two years.

 

What will you be working with?

Your work may include:

• Analog and mixed-signal circuit design
• Schematic and PCB design
• Embedded hardware and component selection
• Prototyping and technical concept evaluation
• Testing, measurement, troubleshooting and verification
• EMC/EMI and noise mitigation, including filtering, grounding and shielding
• Hardware and system integration
• Development with manufacturability and cost in mind
• Collaboration with suppliers, consultants and specialist resources when required
Because the system will operate in the MRI environment, you will work with technical challenges where the solution may not always be obvious from the outset. A hands-on approach to testing, experimentation and problem-solving will therefore be important.Some testing will take place in real MRI environments, so some travel should be expected.

 

Who are we looking for?

You have a relevant background in electronics, hardware engineering or a related discipline, combined with practical experience developing electronic products or systems.

 

Experience in analog and mixed-signal electronics is particularly interesting to us, ideally combined with schematic and PCB design. At the same time, the role requires technical breadth and an interest in working across disciplines.

 

You should also have strong English communication skills, both written and spoken, and work well in a collaborative, fast-paced development environment.

 

Most importantly, we are looking for someone with the drive to make things happen. Someone who takes ownership of a problem, digs into it and keeps moving when the first approach does not work.

 

We believe you will thrive in this role if you:

• Have a hands-on engineering mindset
• Take initiative and ownership of technical challenges
• Enjoy creating and developing new solutions
• Work independently while collaborating closely with others
• Are comfortable challenging technical decisions and discussing different approaches
• Are curious and willing to work outside a narrowly defined specialist area
• Can balance technical quality with progress, manufacturability and cost
 

Additional experience that would be valuable

Experience or familiarity with any of the following would be an advantage:

• Wireless systems, such as Bluetooth LE and Wi-Fi
• Audio electronics, including ANC and ENC
• RF
• Collaboration with suppliers, consultants and specialist resources
• Design for manufacturability
• Medical devices or regulated product development
• Electronics for demanding electromagnetic environments
• MRI-related technology
• AI-assisted engineering tools and familiarity with agentic AI
Experience with medical devices or electronics for the MRI environment would be highly relevant, but is not a prerequisite.

 

You do not need to tick every box. You may be particularly strong in one area and have broader experience or interest across others. We value strong engineering fundamentals, practical experience and the ability to learn and work across disciplines.

 

Why NordicNeuroLab?

You will join the iMRI initiative at an early stage of the development process and have the opportunity to influence important technical decisions..

 

You will work with challenging technology, where real clinical workflows and the MRI environment shape the engineering challenges.

 

NordicNeuroLab offers a flexible and collaborative working environment, with the opportunity to take on significant technical responsibility and contribute your expertise across different areas of product development.

 

For questions regarding this position, please contact Michelle Kolskår, Head of Sales at Folk AS.

Phone: +47 48 13 66 56 E-mail: michelle@folkas.com

 

Since its establishment in 2004, Folk AS has assisted both Norwegian and international companies in finding highly skilled professionals within technical and administrative disciplines for project-based, temporary, and permanent positions. This is what we do best, and where our expertise lies.

Our core values are: ethical, personal, committed, and flexible.

 

We see opportunities in your competence!

Om arbeidsgiveren:

NordicNeuroLab is a medical technology company based in Bergen, developing and manufacturing advanced solutions for use in MRI environments. The company combines engineering, product development and medical technology to create solutions used by hospitals, universities and research institutions worldwide.

jobs.occupation: FOOD TRUCK TEAM MEMBERS
jobs.description:
Spend season 2027 with us!

FOOD TRUCK TEAM MEMBERS

Flåm, Eidfjord & Norheimsund, Norway

Good food. New faces. A team to be part of. And the Norwegian fjords just outside.

Looking for a season somewhere different? Come and join our food truck teams in Flåm, Eidfjord or Norheimsund. You'll prepare food, meet guests and share busy days with the people working beside you.

Already worked in hospitality? We'd love to hear about it. Taking your first steps? You're welcome too - everyone receives training. Bring a willingness to learn, a friendly approach and the energy to get involved.

Your part in the team

• Get to know our food and prepare dishes using the recipes and training we provide.

• Give guests a warm welcome and friendly, attentive service.

• Help orders reach the right guests smoothly, even when the pace picks up.

• Keep your workstation, equipment and service area clean, tidy and ready to use.

• Follow food hygiene and safety procedures.

• Share the work, help your colleagues and follow your Manager or Site Coordinator's guidance.

You'll feel at home in this role if...

• You enjoy meeting people and want guests to leave with a smile.

• You're reliable, ready to learn and happy to support your colleagues.

• You can stay organised and work efficiently during a busy service.

• You speak English at B2-C1 level.

• You hold a valid category B driving licence - this is required for the role.

• Hospitality experience is welcome, but it isn't essential. We'll train you.

What's waiting for you

• Full-time seasonal work with hourly pay and several contract periods to choose from.

• Training to help you settle into your role and get to know our food.

• The chance to meet new colleagues and work together in Norway's fjord region.

• Help finding accommodation for your season in Norway.

• A staff meal on each working day.

Join our team and spend the season surrounded by Norway's breathtaking fjords! With food trucks in Flåm and other beautiful locations, we're all about great food, friendly faces, and making people feel welcome. We'd love to have you on board and share an unforgettable season together! Send your CV and recomendation: job@grpnorway.com

FOOD TRUCK OPERATIONS MANAGER

Flåm, Norway

Bring your experience, your ideas and your love of working with people. Let's make the 2027 season a great one together.

Good food brings people together - and a good manager helps a team bring its best to every shift. Join us in Flåm to lead our food trucks, with the fjords as the setting for your next season. You'll lead around 12 colleagues across food trucks based in one place. There's room to make the role your own: organise the day, help people grow and put your ideas into practice. You'll report directly to the CEO and work closely with HR.

We'd love to meet a leader who enjoys being part of the action. When service gets busy, you'll be alongside your team - preparing food, serving guests and finding solutions together.
